start_notice: A historical mission with fictional return decisions and alternate outcomes.

nodes.title: Mission briefing
nodes.text: Armstrong and Scott will rendezvous and dock with Agena. Before launch, you have time for two extra ground rehearsals: short practice runs on the communications loops, with controllers passing a report or instruction and checking that the right desk received it. The crew's training and mission rules are already in place; these exercises prepare the people in your room to work together under pressure.

nodes.prompt: Choose up to two supplemental ground rehearsals.
nodes.text: In the contact drill, Houston CAPCOM and a tracking-ship CAPCOM practice sending an instruction, reading it back, and confirming receipt to FLIGHT. In the recovery drill, Elias and the Department of Defense recovery coordinator practice passing the aircraft's location report to the ship and confirming who sends the pickup instruction. In the systems drill, Mara calls a low-propellant warning to FLIGHT and CAPCOM together, then passes her recommended response before the next entry task begins.

options.intent: Rehearse sending an instruction and confirming its receipt.
options.cost: Uses one of your two rehearsal opportunities.
options.uncertainty: A missed pass can still leave the instruction waiting for radio contact.
options.attraction: CAPCOM and the tracking station practice the readback before a time-critical call.

options.intent: Rehearse passing the pickup instruction from the recovery desk to the ship.
options.cost: Uses one of your two rehearsal opportunities.
options.uncertainty: The crew may still face a long wait if the nearest ship is far away.
options.attraction: Elias and the DoD coordinator settle who sends the pickup call before the recovery begins.

options.intent: Rehearse calling a low RCS propellant warning to FLIGHT and CAPCOM.
options.cost: Uses one of your two rehearsal opportunities.
options.uncertainty: The warning may arrive before Mara knows what caused it.
options.attraction: Mara practices getting her warning and recommended response to both desks promptly.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: Flight, docking is confirmed. We'll check with the crew again on the next pass.

nodes.title: Loss of contact
nodes.text: The scheduled tracking pass has ended. There's no new report from the spacecraft.

nodes.title: We'll have to wait for contact.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: Flight, we've lost the signal. The crew were docked on the last report. We'll call them at the next station.
CAPCOM has left the next report's receipt blank. Nothing new has come through.

answer.speaker: g8-capcom
answer.text: They confirmed docking before we lost contact. We can't confirm their present attitude or what they're doing now.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: Flight, Coastal Sentry Quebec has an emergency call. They're undocked and rolling out of control. The crew are working to stop it.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: They've regained control using the reentry thrusters. They've used substantial propellant from both RCS rings. That means we terminate the mission.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: Mara gives FLIGHT and CAPCOM the warning together, as rehearsed. The cause of the failure still isn't confirmed.

nodes.title: The rule
nodes.prompt: Terminate the mission after RCS use.

options.intent: Terminate the remaining mission and prepare the contingency return.
options.cost: The remaining docking work and EVA are canceled.
options.uncertainty: The room still needs to confirm the return plan and recovery support.
options.unavailable_reason: Requires the termination rule and the stabilization report.
options.attraction: Bring the crew home under the mission's contingency rules.

nodes.hint: Read the flight rule and the crew's stabilization report before confirming the return order.

nodes.title: Return planning
nodes.prompt: Bring them down now and leave them waiting at sea, or keep them in orbit with less propellant for entry?

lines.speaker: g8-flight-dynamics
lines.text: Two return opportunities. The first gets them down sooner. The second puts the recovery force closer. We can't have both.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: Their condition is stable, for now. It might not be after another orbit.

lines.speaker: g8-recovery
lines.text: Every extra minute on the open ocean brings more risk to the crew. Take the later opportunity and the recovery force will be closer.

questions.text: What are the risks of an earlier return?

answer.speaker: g8-recovery
answer.text: The nearest ship is hours away. They'll be waiting in the capsule, in darkness, with the sea wearing them down. Air support helps, but it doesn't make the ship any closer.

questions.text: What are the risks of another orbit?

answer.speaker: g8-systems
answer.text: They'll spend another orbit in a damaged spacecraft. RCS propellant is already low; they need it to control their attitude during entry. If the warning or our instruction arrives late, they'll have less time to act.

options.intent: Bring them down at the earlier opportunity.
options.attraction: Mara backs ending their time aboard the damaged spacecraft sooner.
options.cost: The nearest ship is hours away. The crew will wait in the capsule at sea, in darkness, growing exhausted before pickup.
options.uncertainty: Confusion over the pickup call could leave them waiting even longer.
options.unavailable_reason: The contingency return has not been directed.

options.intent: Take the later opportunity after one more orbit.
options.attraction: Elias backs landing closer to the recovery force for a quicker pickup.
options.cost: The crew stay aboard as their RCS propellant becomes critically low. Mara must get the warning and entry recommendation through promptly.
options.uncertainty: A delayed warning or repeated instruction could force the crew to rush the entry preparations.
options.unavailable_reason: The contingency return has not been directed.

effects.label: Ordered the later return after one more orbit

nodes.hint: Ask Glen's questions and read each card's risks before choosing a return opportunity.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: Splashdown confirmed. Both crew members responding.

lines.speaker: g8-recovery
lines.text: They're down. We still have to get the ship to them.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: Flight, RCS propellant is critically low. They still need those thrusters for entry.

resolutions.text: The desks first settled who would send the pickup instruction, then called again to confirm receipt. That delayed the team's approach. By the time help reaches the capsule, both crew members are badly exhausted and need assistance getting aboard.
One call needed clarification or a repeat before the pickup team could proceed. The delay added to the crew's long wait at sea. Both are exhausted, but the team brings them aboard.

The pickup instruction reached the right desk and its receipt was confirmed on the first call. The team approaches without an additional delay. The sea wait has still worn the crew down; both are brought aboard.

Mara repeated the warning, and CAPCOM had to ask again for confirmation of the entry instruction. The delays left the crew rushing their final preparations with little RCS propellant remaining. They complete entry and reach the nearby recovery force visibly spent.

effects.label: Entry preparations rushed after two repeated calls

resolutions.text: One call had to be repeated before the room could confirm the entry instruction had been received. The crew completed their preparations under pressure, with little RCS propellant left. They reach the nearby recovery force tired but responsive.

effects.label: Entry preparations delayed by a repeated call

resolutions.text: Mara's warning reached FLIGHT and CAPCOM together, and the entry instruction was confirmed on the first call. RCS propellant remained critically low through entry. The crew reach the nearby recovery force tired but responsive.

nodes.title: Standing procedure

options.intent: Make every report say what's been confirmed and what's still unknown.
options.cost: You can make only one procedure the standing requirement.
options.uncertainty: The next tracking pass may still leave important questions unanswered.
options.unavailable_reason: Requires the recovered crew and the recorded relationship response.
options.attraction: Give the room a clear record of what was known and when.

options.intent: Put aircraft support, ship arrival, and confirmation of each on one recovery sheet.
options.cost: You can make only one procedure the standing requirement.
options.uncertainty: A correctly recorded request may still reach a ship too far away to help quickly.
options.unavailable_reason: Requires the recovered crew and the recorded relationship response.
options.attraction: Let the recovery desk check available help against the time the crew will spend at sea.

nodes.hint: Read what each procedure changes, then choose the one you want to carry into the next mission.

nodes.title: Who carries the blame?
nodes.text: They came home. Now the argument moves from the flight room to the astronaut office. Some call the crew's judgment into question. Others ask what the ground failed to prepare for. Your position will tell the crews whether this room stands behind them when the checklist runs out.

nodes.title: Who carries the blame?

options.intent: Side with Cunningham and Stafford and blame the crew's handling of the emergency.
options.statement: I agree with the criticism. Armstrong and Scott's handling of the emergency deserves the blame.
options.attraction: Gain Cunningham and Stafford's support by backing their criticism.
options.cost: Armstrong and Scott lose trust in Glen, and division within the astronaut corps deepens.
options.uncertainty: The analysis has cleared the crew; your endorsement may prolong the argument rather than settle it.
options.unavailable_reason: Requires the recovered crew, the recorded relationship response, one baseline lesson, the post-flight context, and no prior stance.

effects.label: Glen sided with the crew's critics

options.intent: Accept responsibility for the ground's lack of docked-flight contingency procedures.
options.subtitle: Ground contingency procedures
options.statement: The ground didn't have enough contingency procedures for the docked phase. That's our failure, and we'll correct it. I won't blame Armstrong and Scott for bringing the spacecraft home.
options.attraction: Back the crew and commission procedures for emergencies while docked.
options.cost: Glen publicly accepts responsibility for a failure in the ground organization.
options.uncertainty: Cunningham and Stafford may keep their objections even after the ground begins corrective work.
options.unavailable_reason: Requires the recovered crew, the recorded relationship response, one baseline lesson, the post-flight context, and no prior stance.

effects.label: Glen took responsibility for the ground contingency gap

nodes.hint: Read the post-flight findings and both positions, then choose the statement Glen will make.

resolutions.text: Cunningham and Stafford welcome your support. Armstrong and Scott lose confidence in you. The disagreement now divides the astronaut corps more deeply, with its flight director backing the crew's critics.

resolutions.text: You accept responsibility for the missing ground procedures. Armstrong and Scott's confidence in you strengthens. The critics haven't withdrawn their objections, but the ground team begins work on docked-flight contingencies.

outcomes.title: Crew recovered — earlier return, punishing sea wait
outcomes.result_line: Both crew members are back aboard, badly exhausted after the sea wait. Delays in the pickup calls made an already hard recovery worse.

outcomes.title: Crew recovered — earlier return, difficult pickup
outcomes.result_line: Both crew members are back aboard after a difficult pickup. A call that needed clarification or repeating added to their exhaustion.

outcomes.title: Crew recovered — earlier return, coordinated pickup
outcomes.result_line: The mission ended early, but the pickup was coordinated without an additional delay. Both crew members are aboard, worn down by the wait at sea.

outcomes.title: Crew recovered — extra orbit, rushed entry
outcomes.result_line: Both crew members are back after rushed entry preparations with little RCS propellant remaining. Repeated calls squeezed the time they had to get ready.

outcomes.title: Crew recovered — extra orbit, difficult entry preparations
outcomes.result_line: Both crew members are back after difficult entry preparations. A delayed warning or repeated instruction made the return harder.

outcomes.title: Crew recovered — extra orbit, prompt warning response
outcomes.result_line: The mission ended early, but the warning and entry instruction reached the crew promptly. Both crew members are back after an orderly response with little RCS propellant remaining.

debrief.text: Docking was achieved. The remaining objectives were terminated. Both crew members were recovered alive.
You chose to end spacecraft exposure sooner and accepted a prolonged sea recovery.
You chose another orbit to land closer to the recovery force. The crew completed entry with critically low RCS propellant.
The recovery drill established who would send the pickup instruction. The desks didn't need to settle that during pickup; the ship still had to cover the same distance.
The systems drill helped Mara get her warning to FLIGHT and CAPCOM together. She didn't have to repeat the assessment; the crew still had little RCS propellant left.
The contact drill helped CAPCOM confirm receipt on the first call. The room didn't need to ask again during the return.
Calls that needed clarification or repeating delayed the pickup or squeezed the crew's entry preparations. The crew-condition report records the result.
Elias's response is recorded above. The next mission must include a recovery rehearsal; you'll choose its companion exercise.
Mara's response is recorded above. The next mission must include a systems-warning rehearsal; you'll choose its companion exercise.
You added report timing and confirmation to the procedures binder.
You carried recovery cross-checking into the procedures binder.
You endorsed the criticism of Armstrong and Scott. Cunningham and Stafford's support grew, both crew members lost trust in you, and the astronaut corps became more divided.
You accepted responsibility for the missing ground procedures. The crew's trust in you grew, and you commissioned docked-flight contingency work.

Return timing — Historically, Gemini VIII landed in the western Pacific during its seventh revolution and the crew awaited USS Leonard F. Mason. You chose the game's earlier return. The particular ship delay, darkness, crew exhaustion, and rehearsal-dependent pickup sequence are alternate events, not a reconstruction of that recovery.

debrief.text: Return timing — You took the later opportunity, as history did: Gemini VIII landed in the western Pacific on its seventh revolution and the crew awaited USS Leonard F. Mason. The propellant warning, the closer pickup, and the crew-condition sequence on this route are dramatized, not a reconstruction of that recovery.

plates.title: LEARNING TO FLY TOGETHER
plates.caption: Gemini's two-person missions are teaching NASA how to work in orbit: stay longer, meet another spacecraft, and dock. Those are skills Apollo will need for the journey to the Moon.

plates.title: THE CREW
plates.caption: Command pilot Neil Armstrong and pilot David Scott are flying Gemini VIII. Their mission calls for docking with an Agena target vehicle and a spacewalk by Scott.

plates.title: 16 MARCH 1966
plates.caption: The Agena launches first. A Titan II then lifts Armstrong and Scott from Cape Kennedy, beginning the chase toward their target in orbit.

plates.title: RENDEZVOUS AND DOCKING
plates.caption: Gemini VIII reaches the Agena, and Armstrong brings the two vehicles together. It's the first docking of two spacecraft in Earth orbit.

plates.title: BEYOND THE NEXT CONTACT
plates.caption: The spacecraft are joined, but Houston won't have continuous radio contact. The room will have to separate its last confirmed report from whatever happens beyond the next station's reach.

prologue.history_note: The Manned Spacecraft Center was renamed the Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center in 1973.
prologue.interpretation: The prologue is an illustrated mission overview, then an explicit return to earlier mission preparation. Staging, lighting and motion are artistic interpretations; the inflection caption is original scene-setting prose, not a transcript.
